text.p: Shares listed by Mexican construction companies Empresas ICA and Grupo Tribasa were sharply up in late trade on the Mexican bourse on Friday.
Traders and analyst said the market was buying on the possibility a rescue plan for troubled highway concessions would be announced soon by the government.
Tribasa nominal shares were up 1.55 pesos to 20.55 pesos, while ICA nominal shares had climbed 6.40 pesos to 120.00 pesos.
"The stocks are smoking; one brokerage is covering shorts in the stock, but that is not why they are driving the market, but rather because of the highway plan," a floor trader said.
Dealers noted that Mexico's Minister of Communications and Transportation Carlos Ruiz suggested on Thursday a rescue plan could be unveiled at the beginning of July.
